document_info.file_name: 05. Systematic review of land change stakeholders and undelying causes in Sumatra and Kalimantan.pdf

extracted_stakeholders.name: Indonesian Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: Supports large-scale land use through policies and regulates agricultural and forestry sectors.

extracted_stakeholders.name: IPB University
extracted_stakeholders.role: Involved in the research and review of land change driving forces and actors.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Central and District Governments
extracted_stakeholders.role: Decision-making actors in land management and allocation.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Center for International Forestry Research (CIFOR)
extracted_stakeholders.role: Conducts research and provides data on forestry and land-use changes.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Large Companies
extracted_stakeholders.role: Engage in large-scale agricultural and forestry activities, contributing to land-use change.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Local Communities
extracted_stakeholders.role: Manage small-scale agricultural land and participate in land use and change.

extracted_factors.Label: Oil Palm Expansion
extracted_factors.Description: The expansion of oil palm plantations is a leading direct cause of land change, driven by both large companies and independent farmers in Sumatra and Kalimantan.

extracted_factors.Label: Property Rights Issues
extracted_factors.Description: Ambiguities and conflicts over land ownership and management rights, leading to deforestation and land use change.

extracted_factors.Label: Lack of Institutional Capacity
extracted_factors.Description: Government institutions are unable to effectively enforce land use regulations, leading to unmanaged land changes.

extracted_factors.Label: Transmigration Policy
extracted_factors.Description: Government policy facilitating the relocation of populations for agricultural development, contributing to land change dynamics.

extracted_factors.Label: Agricultural and Forestry Policies
extracted_factors.Description: Policies supporting large-scale agricultural and forestry expansions as a means to boost economic growth.

extracted_pain_points.description: Conflicts and ambiguities regarding land ownership and land rights between the government, companies, and local communities.
Weak enforcement of land-use regulations and overlapping regulatory responsibilities between government institutions.
Negative social impacts on local communities including displacement and lack of recognition of traditional land rights.
Environmental degradation resulting from large-scale land conversion for agriculture and forestry, including deforestation and biodiversity loss.
